seo.h1: Dubu Jorim: Spicy Korean Braised Tofu (Vegetarian Recipe)

How to Make Dubu Jorim (Step-by-Step Guide)
seo.imageAlt: A close-up of a bowl of Dubu Jorim, spicy Korean braised tofu, garnished with green onions and sesame seeds.
seo.imageCaption: Our delicious Dubu Jorim, a flavorful and spicy Korean braised tofu dish that's perfect for a vegetarian meal.

description: Dubu Jorim is a beloved Korean dish featuring firm tofu braised in a savory, spicy, and slightly sweet sauce. This vegetarian delight offers a comforting warmth and rich flavors, making it a perfect side dish or light main course. Each bite delivers a delightful blend of gochujang heat and umami goodness, making it incredibly satisfying.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tofu
instructions.text: Drain the tofu block well. Wrap it in a few layers of paper towels or a clean kitchen towel and place a heavy object on top for 20-30 minutes to press out excess water. This helps the tofu absorb flavors better and prevents it from crumbling.

instructions.title: Slice and Fry Tofu
instructions.text: Once pressed, slice the tofu into 1/2 inch thick rectangular pieces. Heat vegetable oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Pan-fry the tofu slices until golden brown and slightly crispy on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Make the Braising Sauce
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine soy sauce, gochujang, gochugaru, sesame oil, minced garlic, minced ginger, mirin, sugar or corn syrup, and water or vegetable broth. Mix well until all ingredients are thoroughly combined and the sugar is dissolved.

instructions.title: Braise the Tofu
instructions.text: In the same pan (or a clean one), pour the prepared braising sauce. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Carefully add the pan-fried tofu slices to the simmering sauce, arranging them in a single layer if possible.

instructions.title: Simmer and Reduce
instructions.text: Spoon the sauce over the tofu pieces to coat them evenly. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened and the tofu has absorbed the flavors. Occasionally baste the tofu with the sauce during simmering.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Uncover the pan. If the sauce is too thin, increase heat slightly and simmer uncovered for a few more minutes until desired consistency is reached. Stir in most of the sliced green onions. Transfer the Dubu Jorim to a serving dish, garnish with remaining green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot with rice.

tips: Pressing the tofu thoroughly is crucial. It removes excess water, allowing the tofu to absorb the flavorful braising sauce more effectively and achieve a better texture.
Adjust the amount of gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) to your preferred spice level. For a milder dish, reduce it to half a tablespoon; for extra heat, add a bit more.
Dubu Jorim tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld further. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
